text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures tread water in afternoon trade. The market muted in advance of key data this week, speculation on higher February German unemployment underpins sentiment. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.35, up 0.17 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - gilts recover from an early spate of weakness to end slightly higher on the day. Traders say mood is on the positive side but market subdued ahead of key U.S. releases later in the week. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-01/32, up 06/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future settles below 132 for first time since Feb 13, U.S. bonds weigh. June PIBOR slips as well. Mar 10-yr future 131.98, off 0.44. Vol 97,608. Open 132.22. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.98 down 0.44 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures held on to a modest rise by the close but market seen weak and sentiment nervous with operators watching lira hovering around 1,000 per mark level. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.91 up 0.41 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries steady after release of as-expected NAPM Economists see positive and negative factors offsetting Report removes some worry over scheduled Greenspan remarks. Focus now turns to Greenspan testimony Wednesday. Volume steady following heavy flows prior sessions. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-19/32, down 10/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - Yen bond futures closed easier on Monday after the market's rise in the morning following falls in Tokyo stocks was checked at around 126.50 for the key March and 125.00 for the June. Both buying and selling were technical ahead of a benchmark shift expected on Tuesday. Cash bond activity was slim. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.27, down 0.16 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw Oman launch a larger-than-expected debut Eurobond issue on Monday, a $225 million five-year deal. An active dollar sector saw Walt Disney set a $300 million June 1999 bond, IBM issued a $250 million two-year bond and Suedwest LB set a $150 million four-year bond. CADES is planning a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond. In marks, KfW set a 2.0 billion mark 10-year deal, AHB added 500 million marks to a Jan 2004 bond and Rabobank set a 300 million mark December 2001 bond. BOC Group Plc tapped the sterling sector.
